summary: An independent reviewer that had not seen the work audited the code. It found no look-ahead leak in the signals, outcome rules or walk-forward split. It flagged a crash in the live script, a live probability taken from a different model than the one scoring, failed companies dropped when they moved to over-the-counter trading, tickers reused by new companies, and standard errors that were too small for multi-day holds. All five were fixed before the final run. It also confirmed that daily bars match the regular session: only 43 of 2.26 million intraday checks disagreed.
fixed: live score now comes from the latest walk-forward model, matching the calibration tables
series split when a ticker goes silent 60+ sessions
disclosed_not_fixed: target counts as hit when the high equals it exactly
stop fills at the stop price less slippage even if price gaps through intraday
choosing the best of 4 stops over all out-of-sample years carries mild selection bias; the live log is the true holdout
test years also serve as the signal-confirmation period
